name: Ohio

sales.rateNote: State rate 5.75%; counties and regional transit authorities add permissive local sales taxes on top, so the combined rate depends on the county.

local.levies: counties and regional transit authorities (permissive sales and use taxes)
local.capNote: Local add-ons are set in multiples of 0.05% up to 3%; state + county + transit combined cannot exceed 8.75%. County and transit rate changes may only take effect at the start of a calendar quarter.

groceries.note: Food for human consumption off the premises where sold has been exempt since a 1936 constitutional amendment; restaurant meals, prepared food, soft drinks, alcohol, dietary supplements and tobacco are taxable.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable year-round except during the 3-day back-to-school holiday (items $75 or less).

holidays2026.name: Back-to-school sales tax holiday
holidays2026.items: clothing priced at $75 or less per item; school supplies $20 or less; school instructional materials $20 or less

sales.holidayNote: No expanded holiday on items $500 and under in 2026 (the expanded holiday created by H.B. 33 was not repeated); only the standard back-to-school holiday applies.

useTax.note: Use tax at the same state and county rate is due when sales tax was owed but not collected, e.g. online or out-of-state purchases.

facts.text: Ohio's state sales and use tax rate has been 5.75% since September 1, 2013.
Counties and transit authorities can add up to 3% in 0.05% steps, but the total state + local rate is capped at 8.75%.
Warren County's sales and use tax rate changed effective October 1, 2026; no county rate changes took effect January 1, April 1 or July 1, 2026.
Since 2018 Ohio law sets a permanent back-to-school holiday on the first Friday of August and the following weekend (clothing up to $75, school supplies and instructional materials up to $20).
Prescription glasses and contact lenses have been exempt since July 1, 2019, and pads, tampons and period underwear since April 1, 2020.
A motor vehicle bought in a private (casual) sale is still subject to sales or use tax, paid to the county clerk of courts at title transfer.
H.B. 96 (2025) repealed several sales tax exemptions, and H.B. 366 raised the vendor's license fee from $25 to $50 effective April 9, 2025.
Separate from sales tax, H.B. 519 cuts the state motor fuel tax (normally 38.5 cents/gal gasoline, 47 cents/gal diesel) to near zero from October 4, 2026 through January 2, 2027.

property.levied: local only: school districts, counties, municipalities, townships and special districts; values set by the 88 county auditors under Department of Taxation oversight

assessment.text: Taxable (assessed) value is 35% of true market value (CAUV farmland excepted). County auditors fully reappraise every six years with a triennial update in between; tax reduction factors (H.B. 920) offset value growth on voted levies.

homestead.name: Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: Credit equal to the taxes on up to $29,700 of market value (tax year 2026; $29,000 for 2025) for homeowners 65+ or totally and permanently disabled, and qualifying surviving spouses, with Ohio modified AGI of $41,000 or less (2026; $40,000 for 2025). Service-connected disabled veterans and surviving spouses of public service officers killed in the line of duty get an enhanced $59,400 with no income test.
homestead.applyBy: File form DTE 105A (105I veterans, 105K surviving spouses of officers) with the county auditor on or before December 31 of the tax year.

otherRelief.name: Owner-occupancy credit
otherRelief.text: 2.5% credit on property taxes for a homeowner's primary residence (dwelling plus up to one acre); it, like the 10% non-business credit, does not apply to new or replacement levies passed after September 29, 2013.

otherRelief.name: Local-option homestead exemption (H.B. 96, 2025)
otherRelief.text: County commissioners may adopt an additional homestead exemption equal to the state one, essentially doubling it; it is not reimbursed by the state and only applies if the county authorizes it.

otherRelief.name: Current Agricultural Use Value (CAUV)
otherRelief.text: Farmland of 10+ acres in commercial agriculture (or under 10 acres with $2,500 average gross income) is valued on agricultural use rather than market value.

dueDates.text: Typically two installments: first half in late January or early February, second half in late June or early July; exact dates vary by county.

facts.text: The Ohio Constitution limits unvoted ('inside') millage to 10 mills; because it applies to taxable value (35% of market value) the effective cap is 0.35% of true value.
In tax year 2024 the statewide average effective rate after reduction factors was about 52.44 mills on residential and agricultural property and 66.69 mills on commercial and industrial property.
A 10% non-business credit applies to real property not used primarily in business; the state reimburses local governments for it.
Valuation complaints go to the county Board of Revision and must be filed between January 1 and March 31.
H.B. 186 created an 'inflation cap credit' that limits growth of school levies held at the 20-mill floor; the Department lists it as effective March 20, 2026.
Once approved, the homestead exemption and owner-occupancy credit renew automatically unless eligibility changes.

uncertain: Ohio Revised Code site (codes.ohio.gov) and legislature.ohio.gov were unreachable from this network; statutory facts are taken from Department of Taxation pages and its FY2025 annual report.
Motor vehicle sales tax rate rules (county of titling) not detailed on a page read; otherRates left empty.
H.B. 186 effective date is as stated on the Department's legislation page (March 20, 2026); full enrolled text not read.
Specific county due dates not statewide; only the Department's 'typical' schedule is given.
